subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session exec fields be allowed to override a later stricter global or agent exec security configuration after a Discord session resumes?
rationale: The source reproduction is clear, but the fix changes a security-sensitive precedence contract that current tests intentionally encode as persisted session defaults.

options.title: Make config the security upper bound
options.body: Clamp or clear stored session exec fields when they are less restrictive than current global or agent exec security, with focused upgrade/reset coverage.

options.title: Keep persistence and document reset
options.body: Preserve existing per-session override behavior and document that operators must reset or repair sessions to enforce changed exec policy.

options.title: Add explicit operator reset first
options.body: Ship a session exec reset or doctor repair surface before changing precedence for existing sessions.

recommendation.title: Make config the security upper bound
recommendation.body: Clamp or clear stored session exec fields when they are less restrictive than current global or agent exec security, with focused upgrade/reset coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The clearest history trail for the focused reply exec override helper and tests points to steipete.
